doc.title: Javon Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Cancelled gigs and advice from Sonny Rollins
summary: Cancellations trickled in; he accepts them since everyone is affected, and Sonny Rollins reminds him there is much to do at home.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: As far as loss of gigs and concerts, did your cancellations come all at once or did you sort of see it coming and how did you feel about it when certain engagements you had lined up —

Right, well they came, Monk, as a trickling in the beginning, certain concerts month by month and then there was just several months regarding to the summer just all being cancelled. My reaction is I can’t get mad because everyone is experiencing this, whether in the sports arena, in the performance arena, Broadway theater. So it’s not as if it’s an isolated thing against me, the lone wolf jazz saxophonist, just for everyone. So I just have to kind of accept it and use this opportunity to find some other things to do which — I had a conversation with Sonny Rollins about this situation by phone and he said, “Remember there’s always a lot to do in the house.” And he is so right. I mean there’s so much actually that you can do when you’re inside, is what he said to me. So trying to take advantage of that with some reading. Actually I’ve been revisiting so many CDs and recordings that I’ve had time to look at and obviously you can put more time in with your music and try to hone that skill or that craft, and maybe some compositions, some writing. And then again, just try to keep yourself ready for the opportunities when they
will come back. But never have I gotten upset about it, because again, everyone is involved in it. Every sect of life.

Yes. And I know some musicians that, when those things first started to come trickling in they were posting things on FaceBook or whatever that almost sounded like they were being singled out, the way they were speaking like. But as you say, everybody is in the same position. So have you, how far ahead have people cancelled?
